questions.prompt: Why does `FOR r IN (...) LOOP UPDATE tbl ...; END LOOP;` perform poorly on 100,000 rows compared to a single SQL `UPDATE` or `BULK COLLECT`/`FORALL`?

options.text: PL/SQL loops use too much CPU
Every row triggers a separate context switch between the PL/SQL engine and the SQL engine, plus extra redo/undo overhead

questions.prompt: Why is `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ''' || p_name || ''''` a critical vulnerability AND performance bug?

options.text: Concatenating `p_name` enables SQL injection AND prevents bind-variable cursor sharing (causing hard-parse CPU/library-cache latch contention!)

code.source:
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = :1'
  INTO l_id USING p_name;

questions.prompt: When `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` needs a dynamic table or column name (which bind variables CANNOT parameterize), how should you sanitize it?

options.text: Validate against `DBMS_ASSERT.SIMPLE_SQL_NAME` / `SQL_OBJECT_NAME` or an explicit allowlist of known table names

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Must end with an explicit `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` before returning, or Oracle raises `ORA-06519`
Cannot see uncommitted changes made by the caller's outer transaction
Automatically rolls back if the caller's outer transaction rolls back (no—that's why it's dangerous for business data!)
Suspends the caller's transaction so the subprogram can `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` its own independent transaction (ideal for error/audit logging)

questions.prompt: What does `PRAGMA UDF` (Oracle 12c+) on a PL/SQL function optimize?

options.text: Tells the compiler the function is primarily called from SQL `SELECT`/`WHERE` clauses, reducing SQL-to-PL/SQL call overhead

questions.prompt: What is a `PIPELINED` table function (`FUNCTION gen_rows RETURN t_tab PIPELINED`) used for?

options.text: Streaming rows out incrementally via `PIPE ROW(rec)` as they are produced, without materializing the whole collection in PGA memory

questions.prompt: What does `ORA-04068: existing state of packages has been discarded` mean in a long-running connection pool?

options.text: A stateful package (one with package-level variables) was recompiled while pooled sessions still held old state, causing the next call to fail once

questions.prompt: What does Edition-Based Redefinition (EBR) in Oracle enable?

options.text: Zero-downtime online upgrades of PL/SQL packages, views, and triggers in a new Edition while active sessions continue on the old Edition

questions.prompt: What does `ALTER SESSION SET PLSQL_WARNINGS = 'ENABLE:ALL';` help catch during CI/compilation?

options.text: Unreachable code, implicit conversions, `WHEN OTHERS` without `RAISE`, and performance anti-patterns at compile time

questions.prompt: What does `PLSQL_OPTIMIZE_LEVEL = 2` (default) automatically do for cursor `FOR` loops?

options.text: Silently array-fetches 100 rows at a time (`BULK COLLECT` optimization) under the hood!

questions.prompt: Why can `DETERMINISTIC` on a function cause wrong results if misused?

options.text: You promise Oracle the function always returns the exact same output for the same inputs (no `SYSDATE`, no table reads)—misuse lets SQL reuse stale cached results or build invalid function-based indexes

questions.prompt: What does `DBMS_PROFILER` or `DBMS_HPROF` (Hierarchical Profiler) measure?

options.text: Line-by-line / subprogram-level execution time and call counts inside PL/SQL to pinpoint bottlenecks

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `WITH FUNCTION` (Oracle 12c+ inline PL/SQL in SQL). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Lets you define a temporary PL/SQL helper function directly inside a `WITH` clause of a `SELECT` query
Runs with reduced context-switch overhead (`PRAGMA UDF`-like)
Avoids creating permanent schema objects for one-off/ad-hoc SQL queries
Automatically persists the function into `USER_OBJECTS` permanently

questions.prompt: What is a classic deadlock cause in concurrent PL/SQL transactions?

options.text: Session 1 updates row A then row B while Session 2 updates row B then row A (`ORA-00060`)

questions.prompt: What does `ORA-00060: deadlock detected while waiting for resource` do to the transaction?

options.text: Oracle rolls back the single deadlocked *statement* (not the whole transaction) and raises `ORA-00060`—so your handler should `ROLLBACK` or retry cleanly

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid calling a PL/SQL function in a `WHERE` clause on an indexed column (`WHERE normalize(email) = :1`) without a Function-Based Index?

options.text: Applying a function to an unindexed column prevents Oracle from using a normal B-tree index on `email`, forcing a full table scan

questions.prompt: What does `DBMS_SCHEDULER` replace in modern Oracle compared to legacy `DBMS_JOB`?

options.text: Enterprise job scheduling with calendar expressions, job chains, credential management, resource-manager integration, and run history

questions.prompt: What does `ACCESSIBLE BY (PACKAGE my_internal_api)` (Oracle 12c+ white-list clause) on a package or subprogram enforce?

options.text: Restricts which specific PL/SQL units are allowed to call it at compile time—great for internal helper packages

code.source: CREATE PACKAGE helper ACCESSIBLE BY (PACKAGE orders_api) AS ...

questions.prompt: What does `PL/SQL` `CLOB` / `BLOB` temporary LOB management require when creating temp LOBs via `DBMS_LOB.CREATETEMPORARY` in a loop?

options.text: Always free them with `DBMS_LOB.FREETEMPORARY` when done (or reuse one) to avoid leaking temporary tablespace!

questions.prompt: What does `PARALLEL_ENABLE` on a `PIPELINED` function allow?

options.text: Allows Oracle Parallel Query (`PX` slaves) to execute the pipelined table function across partitioned cursor streams (`PARTITION p BY HASH(...)`)

questions.prompt: What is a subtle risk of implicit data-type conversion in SQL/PLSQL (`WHERE varchar_id = 123`)?

options.text: Oracle converts the *column* `TO_NUMBER(varchar_id) = 123`, disabling any index on `varchar_id` AND risking `ORA-01722: invalid number`!

questions.prompt: What does `DBMS_LOCK.ALLOCATE_UNIQUE` + `DBMS_LOCK.REQUEST` provide?

options.text: Application-level named advisory distributed locks across Oracle sessions (for serializing critical batch jobs)

questions.prompt: Select all best practices for high-performance, maintainable PL/SQL in production. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use `WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL;` and `AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION` for every business DML procedure
Set-based SQL (`INSERT...SELECT`, `MERGE`, `UPDATE`) first; `BULK COLLECT` + `FORALL` second; row-by-row loops last
Always use bind variables in `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` / `OPEN ... FOR ... USING`
Instrument jobs with `DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO` and log errors with `FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE`

questions.prompt: What does `OPEN rc FOR 'SELECT * FROM emp WHERE dept = :1' USING p_dept;` do?

options.text: Opens a `SYS_REFCURSOR` using dynamic SQL safely with bind variable `:1`

code.source: OPEN rc FOR l_sql USING p_dept_id;

questions.prompt: What does `SQLERRM` truncation or `FORMAT_ERROR_STACK` vs `SQLERRM` differ on?

options.text: `DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK` returns the complete error stack without `SQLERRM`'s 512-byte truncation limit

questions.prompt: What does `utPLSQL` provide for Oracle PL/SQL teams?

options.text: An open-source unit-testing framework (xUnit-style annotations `--%test`, `--%suite`, matchers, coverage) for CI/CD

questions.prompt: What does `INDICES OF` vs `VALUES OF` in `FORALL` allow?

options.text: `INDICES OF` iterates over existing keys of a sparse collection; `VALUES OF` uses the *values* of an index-mapping collection as subscripts into another collection

questions.prompt: Why does `SELECT *` inside production PL/SQL cursors (`CURSOR c IS SELECT * FROM orders`) carry maintenance risk?

options.text: Adding/reordering columns can break positional `FETCH INTO` variable lists or fetch wide unused `CLOB`/`BLOB` columns unnecessarily

questions.prompt: What does `PRAGMA INLINE(subprogram, 'YES')` (Oracle 11g+) do?

options.text: Hints the PL/SQL optimizer to inline a small hot subprogram call inside a loop

questions.prompt: What happens when `COMMIT WRITE BATCH NOWAIT` is abused instead of default `COMMIT`?

options.text: Skips waiting for redo log flush to disk, risking loss of committed transactions on instance crash (never use for financial/critical data!)

options.text: When the number of bind variables or `SELECT` list columns is unknown at compile time (e.g., generic CSV exporter)

questions.prompt: What does `DBMS_ERRLOG.CREATE_ERROR_LOG` + `INSERT INTO ... SELECT ... LOG ERRORS REJECT LIMIT UNLIMITED` do?

options.text: Logs failing rows of a pure SQL `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`MERGE` into an error-logging table without aborting the set-based SQL statement

questions.prompt: Why is `COUNT(*)` to check existence (`SELECT COUNT(*) INTO l_cnt FROM t WHERE ...; IF l_cnt > 0`) slower than `SELECT 1 ... WHERE EXISTS` or `ROWNUM = 1`?

options.text: `COUNT(*)` scans *all* matching rows, whereas `ROWNUM = 1` / `FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY` stops immediately on the first match

code.source:
SELECT COUNT(*) INTO l_found FROM DUAL
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE id = p_id);
